Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Baan Thai** | 1400 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, rice paper) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | | **Siam Thai** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai”
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (no meat, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | | **Thai Orchid** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai”
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [thaiorchid.com](https://www.thaiorchid.com) | | **Siam Square** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai”
• “Vegetarian Green Curry”
• “Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai” (no chicken, optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | | **Siam Thai Bistro** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai”
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry”
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [siamthais.com](https://www.siamthais.com) | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants are located on the same block (1400‑1220 W 18th St), so you can walk between them if you’d like to try a few different dishes. They’re all in the West Loop/West Town area, which is a popular dining district in Chicago. ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining at Thai Restaurants 1. **Ask for “No Egg” or “No Fish Sauce”** – Many Thai dishes contain eggs or fish sauce. Most restaurants will happily omit these ingredients for you. 2. **Request “Tofu” or “Vegetable” Versions** – If a dish is listed as “Chicken” or “Beef,” ask if they can substitute tofu or extra vegetables. 3. **Look for “Vegetarian” or “Vegan” Labels** – Some menus now include a separate vegetarian section or a “V” icon next to vegetarian-friendly items. 4. **Check Online Menus** – Most of the restaurants above list their menus online, often with vegetarian options clearly marked. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more detailed menu information or reservations, let me know.
